summary: Rental car broken into at a viewpoint near Sintra
story: On July 14 I parked my rental car at a viewpoint near Sintra and walked up to the gardens for about an hour. The car was locked. When I came back the rear window was smashed and my things were gone from inside the car: my backpack with my laptop and a jacket, my prescription sunglasses and a portable charger. I went to the police that afternoon and they took down everything. The rental company has since charged me for the window, so I am claiming that bill too. Everything I lost is listed below with the receipts.

summary: Disc pain and sciatica needing an emergency admission in Santiago
story: On August 6 I woke in my hotel in Santiago with severe pain down my left leg and could not stand. The hotel called an ambulance and I was admitted overnight and had an MRI. They told me it was a herniated disc. I saw my doctor once back in April about my back, and I have not had an appointment since. Once I got home I had four physiotherapy sessions, which I have also listed. I have attached everything the hospital gave me.

summary: Checked ski bag did not arrive on a late-running flight to Valbrenna; replacement ski clothes bought before it was delivered the next day
story: My flight out for a week of skiing ran late, and we didn't get in until well into the evening of February 14. My big duffel with all my ski clothes never came off the carousel. I filed a report at the airline desk before I left the airport, and they gave me a small cash advance for toiletries. I had a group lesson booked for 9 the next morning and nothing warm to wear. There was no word on the bag overnight, so I was at the sports shop in the village when it opened and bought a jacket, ski pants, base layers, gloves and socks so I could make the lesson. The bag didn't turn up at the hotel until the next day, after I'd already bought everything. I'm claiming what I spent and I've attached the receipt and the airline report.

summary: Both passports lost on the way to the cruise port, replaced at the port passport agency on embarkation day
story: We drove down from Columbus to Port Calder for our Seabright cruise and stayed the night near the terminal. I had checked the travel folder with both passports before we left home and put it in my backpack. When we unpacked at the hotel that night the folder was gone. We think it slipped out at one of the rest stops along the highway. We called the rest stops and the highway patrol, but nobody had handed it in. First thing on embarkation morning we took a taxi to the passport agency in town, got photos done across the street and applied for emergency passports. They were ready before lunch, we took a taxi back to the hotel for our bags and we made it on board before the ship sailed. I am claiming the passport fees, the photos and the taxis.

summary: Backpack stolen from a locked rental car at a fuel station
story: On September 8 I stopped for fuel at a station outside Impruneta. I locked the rental car and went inside to pay. I was gone maybe five minutes. When I came back the car had been broken into and my backpack was gone. It had my passport, my laptop, some cash and some clothes in it. The station attendant helped me call the police and I made a report straight away. I also told the rental company, because the rental came with some cover for belongings, and they have since settled part of it. The next day I took a taxi to the US Consulate in Florence, had new passport photos taken and paid for an emergency passport so I could fly home. I am claiming for everything I lost and what the passport cost me.

summary: Ear injury from scuba diving on the third day of the trip, treated at a local clinic with a follow-up visit, and a hearing check at home
story: On the third day of my trip I went scuba diving with a local dive shop at Parrotfish Garden. On the way down I had trouble clearing my left ear. By the time we got back to the boat it was very painful and my hearing on that side was muffled. The dive shop drove me to the clinic in town that afternoon. The doctor said it was ear barotrauma, gave me medicine and told me not to dive again on the trip. She asked me to come back two days later so she could check it, and I did. It was getting better. When I got home I still felt a little blocked, so I had a hearing test at an audiology clinic on February 18. Everything was fine by then. I am claiming the two clinic visits in Honduras and the hearing test at home.

summary: Dislocated shoulder on a canyon ride with Talon Excursions
story: On November 8 I went on what I can only call an extreme canyon ride with Talon Excursions outside Queenstown. When I booked at their hire desk, the woman there asked about my insurance and said the ride 'needs adventure cover'. I told her I just had ordinary travel insurance and went anyway, because everyone said it was the best thing in Queenstown. Partway down the canyon we did one of the fast spins, I was thrown sideways against the rail and my right shoulder came out. Talon's staff drove me straight to the hospital in town, where they put it back under sedation and kept me in overnight. I left the next day in a brace with painkillers. Once I was home in Columbus I had a physio session, which I've added. I paid the hospital in full before I left, and I've since had some money back from a New Zealand accident scheme the hospital signed me up for. I'm claiming the hospital bills and the physio. After what the desk told me I'm half expecting a no.

summary: Broken ankle on landing after a scenic flight with Aerie Adventures near Interlaken
story: On February 11, my fifth day in the Bernese Oberland, I booked a sightseeing flight with a local company called Aerie Adventures. The views over the two lakes and the mountains were incredible. We came in to land in Interlaken a little faster than expected, and when we touched down my right foot went under me and I heard a crack in my ankle. Staff from the company called an ambulance and I was taken to the hospital in Interlaken. They X-rayed it, said the ankle was broken, set it and put it in a splint, and sent me back to my hotel that night with crutches and a walking boot. I managed the rest of the trip slowly and flew home on my original date. I paid the hospital on my card before I left and am claiming the bill.

summary: Bag with phone, laptop and cash missing after driving between two hotels
story: On the morning of August 12 I checked out of the Albergo Corallina in Ravello Marina and loaded my rental car in front of the hotel. Then I drove about four hours to my next hotel in Castelbruno. When I unpacked there that evening, my small black shoulder bag was not in the car. It had my phone, my laptop and about $90 in cash in it. I think I either left it on the pavement by the hotel entrance while I was loading the car, or somebody took it while I was going back and forth. I did not report it to the police or call the first hotel. I didn't think there was any point, because I was hours away by then and I was sure nobody would hand in a phone and a laptop. I bought a cheap phone the next day so I could keep traveling. I would like to claim for the bag's contents.

summary: Phone taken from the front desk of a hotel lobby during check-in
story: On September 5 I got to the Hotel Miralbo in Valencia in the late afternoon after a day trip to Xativa. At the front desk I put my phone down on the counter right next to my hand while I filled in and signed the check-in form. The lobby was busy with a tour group. When I finished and reached for it, the phone was gone. The desk clerk checked the camera and saw a man pick it up and walk straight out. The manager was very apologetic and the hotel helped me go to the police that same evening. I bought the phone in March and it was the one thing I really needed on the trip. I am claiming the cost of the phone.

summary: Return flight canceled after an air traffic control failure, home four days late
story: I was due to fly home from Athens on the morning of August 12. When I got to the airport the board showed my flight as canceled, and the airline staff said the air traffic control system had gone down and almost nothing was taking off. The next seat they could give me was on the evening of August 15. Half the airport was trying to find a bed that night, and the only room I could get in the city was at a hotel near Syntagma at $410 a night, so I stayed there for three nights. I ate my meals out and kept the receipts, and I took a taxi in from the airport and another back on the 15th. I landed at home on August 16, four days later than planned, which also meant I missed a concert in Boston on August 13 that I had a ticket for. I am claiming the hotel, the meals, the two taxis and the concert ticket.

story: My wife and I were booked to fly to Cancun on August 21 for a week at the beach. On August 20 Skylark Airways emailed to say every flight to Cancun was cancelled because of the hurricane, and nothing would fly there for days. There was no way to get there, so we cancelled the trip. The airline would not give us anything back because we were on their basic fare, and the hotel only refunded part of what we paid. Altogether we are out a lot of money for a vacation we never got to take. We have kept every email and receipt, and they are all attached.
